readme: Hand verdicts for ops\report-safety-liveness.ps1 (backlog I129). One entry per detector that reaches the clock. The test: freeze every input and advance the clock; LIVENESS if the verdict can move from clean to a finding, SAFETY otherwise. grade EXIT = the finding can move the detector's own exit code, PRINT = printed only. sig is the report's signature of the file's clock evidence: when it changes the verdict reads STALE and must be re-read, never re-stamped unread.

entries.reason: PULL OVERDUE when today passes the schedule's next_pull, and CLOSED when today passes the ad's ad_to; either exits 1
the clock sets the 7 and 30 day reporting windows; the quiet-day target is printed and the exit is always 0
the clock is a window over queue items; an older item drops out, it never adds a finding
reaches the clock only through Write-CoverageRecord's stamp

a not-carried.json entry older than its recheck_days stops suppressing its gap, which can then page (exit 2) when a matching product is at the store: a not-carried verdict is soft state that must be re-checked. The other two clock reads only window out expired ads and rows past the union cliff
STALE when a check's newest recorded coverage is older than its max_age_days ('the check stopped recording'); exit 2 under -Gate
reaches the clock only through Write-CoverageRecord's stamp
the clock dates a 'due in N windows' message and picks today's capture plan for the rotation size; no finding depends on an age
reaches the clock only through Write-CoverageRecord's stamp
STALE LIVE PAGE past 14 days (Test-LivePageStale), printed only for pages already listed as drifted or unpublished; the exit is decided by the drift count. Get-GhostJWT's clock is token time
observations_fresh FAILs when graph.db or its newest observed_at is past 26 or 36 hours (Test-TcInput); the lane is advisory and exits 0
the clock expires baseline names absent 30 days; advancing it removes carried names, never adds a finding
AD COVERAGE GONE when the newest ad file's window has closed and no next ad is in hand, and a same-day browser-capture deferral expires after 25 hours; either exits 1

gap ages are measured on the board's own as-of (Resolve-BoardAsOf reads it off the board filename), so a board that stops being built stops this clock too; the wall clock is used only when no board exists
names Get-RollbackWindow only inside a description string; it never calls it
the clock skips taxonomy files older than MaxTaxonomyAgeDays and names the report; fewer inputs, never a finding
the clock times the run
WARNING when the newest comprehensive Walmart capture is WarnAgeDays old, or a cell's only row nears the union cliff; exits 1, which its header calls advisory and never publish-blocking
reaches the clock only through Get-GhostJWT's token time
the clock only picks which manifest the hub is compared against (today's green verdict or the last shipped one); every finding is a disagreement between two artefacts, not an age
the cmdlet name appears only as data in its pinned list and allowlist
time.time() appears only inside a fixture string
THE FLOOR: the newest event older than FLOOR_DAYS (3) is a finding and exits 2, and an empty bus becomes one after its patience. Write-TcEvent's clock is its producer stamp
the cmdlet appears only inside a fixture string
the clock is a 14-day window over red-gate events and the exit is always 0
the clock stamps a commit message

dated claims older than StaleDays (90) are listed STALE 'for a person, not a verdict'; the exit is decided by the scope-key and paths checks alone (an inert globs:, alwaysApply: or mis-cased paths key, and a paths: entry that matches no tracked file)
